'''Samir H Saker''' is an Egyptian professor of mathematics at the Department of Mathematics, Faculty of Science, [[Mansoura University]], Egypt.  He is the Manager of IT Unit, Faculty of Science, [[Mansoura University]], an elected member of [[American Mathematical Society]] and [[European Mathematical Society]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |last=Samir |first=Saker |title=curriculum vitae |url=http://scholar.cu.edu.eg/jdoe/files/cv8.pdf}}</ref><ref name=":1">{{Cite web |title=Samir Saker |url=https://www.gu.edu.eg/ar/samir-saker/ |access-date=2022-06-18 |website=Galala University |language=ar}}</ref><ref name=":2">{{Cite web |title=Editorial Team {{!}} Open Journal of Engineering Science (ISSN: 2734-2115) |url=https://www.openjournalsnigeria.org.ng/journals/index.php/ojes/about/editorialTeam |access-date=2022-06-18 |website=www.openjournalsnigeria.org.ng}}</ref>

== Early life and education ==
Samir Saker was born January 11, 1971. He obtained his B.Sc. and M. SC in Mathematics from Mansoura University, Egypt in 1993 and 1997 respectively. He won a scholarship to pursue his PhD at [[Adam Mickiewicz University in Poznań|Adam Mickiewicz University]], Poznan, Poland and graduated in 2002.<ref name=":1" /><ref name=":3">{{Cite web |title=Samir H. Saker - Mathematician of the African Diaspora |url=http://www.math.buffalo.edu/mad/PEEPS2/sakir_samir.html |access-date=2022-06-18 |website=www.math.buffalo.edu}}</ref><ref name=":0" />

== Career ==
Samir Saker began his career as a demonstrator  at  Department of Mathematics, Faculty of Science, Mansoura till professorship in the same university.  A year after his B. SC (1994), he was appointed as a demonstrator of mathematics . He became  assistant lecturer in the same institution a year after his M.Sc. (1998). He became a full lecturer in 2003, associate Professor of Mathematics in 2008 and In 2013, he became a  professor.<ref name=":3" /><ref name=":0" /><ref name=":1" />

== Awards and memberships ==
In 2003, Samir Saker won the Shoman Award for Young Arab Scientists in [[Jordan]]. He won USA [[Fulbright scholarship]] to [[Trinity University (Texas)|Trinity University]] in 2004. He won the Egyptian National State Prize award twice; 2005 and 2014 and Amin Lotfy Award in Mathematics in 2009.<ref name=":2" /><ref name=":1" />
